title: Positive unipotent boundaries and their restriction/scalar naturality
statement:
Fix the small coherent profinite site and a coefficient universe containing its objects, morphisms and all section sets below [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], let $\mathcal M_R$ be its internal module category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and let $J,H$ be topological groups. Write $\underline J(S)=C(S,J)$ and $\mathcal A_R(J)$ for internal $R$-modules with a natural $\underline J$-action by linear automorphisms [def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the normalized functors of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-invariants]: $T_J$ is trivial inflation, $\Gamma_{R,J}$ is the invariant subsheaf with its specified inclusion, $L_J=D(T_J)$, $F_J=R\Gamma_{R,J}$ with its canonical computation unit $\alpha_J$, and $L_J\dashv F_J$ is the canonical derived adjunction, with unit $\eta_J$ and counit $\varepsilon_J$. For a continuous homomorphism $u:H\to J$ put $U=D(u^*)$.

Use the normalized cup unit $e_J:R[0]\to F_JR[0]$ and the unipotent connecting-class convention of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-cup, def-sfb-condensed-unipotent-class]. For every additive condensed-group map $a:\underline J\to(R,+)$, the formula $j(x,y)=(x+a(j)y,y)$ gives a natural linear group action on $E_a=R\oplus R$. The first inclusion $i(x)=(x,0)$ and second projection $p(x,y)=y$ form a short exact sequence in $\mathcal A_R(J)$ with trivial regular modules as endpoints. With its canonical short-exact-sequence boundary $\partial_a:R[0]\to R[1]$, the arrow
$$\xi_a=(F_J(\partial_a)\circ e_J)[-1]:R[-1]\longrightarrow F_JR[0]$$
uses the canonical shift comparison and is the positive connecting class $[a]$. Its sectionwise equivariance defect under the underlying splitting $t(y)=(0,y)$ is $jt(1)-t(1)=(a(j),0)$, so its normalized degree-one inhomogeneous cocycle is $+a$.

Restriction by $u:H\to J$ identifies the full short exact sequence, including $i,p,t$, with that for $E_{a\circ u}$, and identifies their canonical boundaries under the localized restriction and shift comparisons. A condensed ring map $\varphi:R\to R'$ gives a morphism from this sequence to the scalar restriction of the sequence for $E_{\varphi\circ a}$: its middle map is $(x,y)\mapsto(\varphi(x),\varphi(y))$ and both endpoint maps are $\varphi$. Its connecting square commutes with the normalized coefficient comparison. Consequently
$$b_u\circ\xi_a=\xi_{a\circ u},\qquad
c_J(\varphi)\circ\xi_a=s_0(\xi_{\varphi\circ a})\circ\varphi[-1],$$
with the canonical scalar shift comparison in the second formula. These are equalities in the ordinary derived category of internal modules. For $a=0$ the class is zero; all conclusions include the trivial group and the zero ring. They assert no acyclicity of underived continuous cochains.

proof.text: On each profinite test object $S$, write $A_j(x,y)=(x+a_S(j)y,y)$. Additivity of $a_S$ gives $A_jA_k(x,y)=(x+(a_S(j)+a_S(k))y,y)=A_{jk}(x,y)$ and $A_1=1$; $A_{j^{-1}}$ is the inverse. Commutativity of $R(S)$ makes $A_j$ $R(S)$-linear. The naturality of $a$ and of ring multiplication makes these maps commute with every restriction in $S$, hence gives the required internal action. Direct calculation gives $A_ji=i$ and $pA_j=p$. The underlying sequence is split exact: $pt=1$, and $ker p$ consists exactly of the pairs $(x,0)$, the image of $i$. Forgetting action detects exactness by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure], so this is a short exact sequence in the action category. The splitting $t$ here is only an underlying-module splitting.

source.place: Paragraph (3), dense-lattice input; agent-written unipotent extension calculation below the returned restriction-calculus steps 11–12

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to this short exact sequence concentrated in degree zero, obtaining its canonical boundary $\partial_a:R[0]\to R[1]$ in the action-derived category. The derived invariants functor is additive and triangulated by [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure], with the specified signed shift comparison. Consequently $F_J(\partial_a)e_J$ is an arrow $R[0]\to(F_JR[0])[1]$, and shifting down gives the displayed arrow $\xi_a$. This is exactly the construction of $[a]$ in [def-sfb-condensed-unipotent-class], using the cup unit of [def-sfb-condensed-derived-cup]; no independent choice of a boundary or of its negative is being made.

proof.text: For the positive normalization, compute the equivariance defect of the fixed underlying lift: $A_jt(y)-t(y)=(a_S(j)y,0)=i(a_S(j)y)$, and in particular $i^{-1}(A_jt(1)-t(1))=a_S(j)$. Thus the normalized inhomogeneous one-cocycle of [def-sfb-condensed-unipotent-class] is $+a_S$, not its negative. It is normalized since $a_S(1)=0$, and satisfies the cocycle equation $a_S(jk)=a_S(j)+a_S(k)$ for the trivial endpoint action. All these equalities commute with base change in $S$. This calculation uses the stated connecting-class convention; it does not identify a continuous-cochain complex with the total derived functor.

proof.text: Under restriction along $u$, the formula becomes $A_{u(h)}(x,y)=(x+(a\circ u)_S(h)y,y)$; the underlying $R\oplus R$, $i$, $p$ and $t$ are literally unchanged. Thus the restricted sequence is the sequence for $a\circ u$. The given $u$ is a continuous group homomorphism, exactly as required by the current statement of [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure]; its restriction is therefore additive and exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-ses-triangle-image] with this exact restriction functor: its termwise localization takes $\partial_a$ to $\partial_{a\circ u}$, including the canonical single-object and shift comparisons. This proves the assertion about the full restricted short exact sequence and its canonical boundary.

proof.text:
By [lem-sfb-condensed-restriction-mate-normalization], the last-arrow square for this triangle is $b_{u,R}[1]F_J(\partial_a)=F_H(U\partial_a)b_{u,R}$. By the unit clause of [lem-sfb-condensed-cup-mate-coherence], $b_{u,R}e_J=e_H$ under the regular-unit identification. Composing the first equality with $e_J$ and using step 4 therefore gives
$$b_{u,R}[1]F_J(\partial_a)e_J=F_H(\partial_{a\circ u})e_H.$$
Shift down by one with the fixed comparisons. Its left side is $b_u\xi_a$ and its right side is $\xi_{a\circ u}$, as claimed. The same comparison that identifies the image triangles identifies their last arrows; there is no appeal to equality of cohomology classes alone.

proof.text:
Put $a'=\varphi\circ a$ and $v=\varphi\oplus\varphi:R\oplus R\to s_J(R'\oplus R')$. Sectionwise,
$$v(A_j(x,y))=(\varphi(x)+\varphi(a(j))\varphi(y),\varphi(y))=A'_j(v(x,y)).$$
It is $R$-linear, commutes with restrictions, and satisfies $vi=i'\varphi$, $p'v=\varphi p$ and $vt=t'\varphi$. Thus $(\varphi,v,\varphi)$ is the claimed morphism of short exact sequences with bottom row scalar-restricted from $R'$. The arbitrary condensed ring map $\varphi$ meets the scalar-restriction clause of [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure], which supplies additivity and exactness without flatness. The exact-functor boundary comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-ses-triangle-image] identifies the bottom boundary with $s_J\partial_{a'}$. The morphism naturality of [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] then gives
$$(s_J\partial_{a'})\varphi=\varphi[1]\partial_a$$
under the canonical scalar single and shift comparisons. No extension of scalars or flatness assertion is used.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, functoriality under a morphism of short exact sequences; Tag 0151 for exact scalar restriction

proof.text:
Write $c=c_J(\varphi)=d_{J,R'}F_J^R(\varphi)$, as specified by [def-sfb-condensed-scalar-tensor]. Apply $F_J^R$ to the boundary square of step 6. Naturality of $d_J$ and its shift compatibility in [lem-sfb-condensed-scalar-restriction-interchange] give
$$c[1]F_J^R(\partial_a)=s_0(F_J^{R'}(\partial_{a'}))c.$$
The algebra-map unit clause of [lem-sfb-condensed-cup-mate-coherence], with scalar lax unit $\varphi$ from [def-sfb-condensed-scalar-tensor], is $ce_J^R=s_0(e_J^{R'})\varphi$. Composing yields
$$c[1]F_J^R(\partial_a)e_J^R=s_0(F_J^{R'}(\partial_{a'})e_J^{R'})\varphi.$$
After shifting down with the canonical scalar comparison this is precisely $c_J(\varphi)\xi_a=s_0(\xi_{\varphi\circ a})\varphi[-1]$. This proves the normalized coefficient connecting square and the asserted derived equality for arbitrary $\varphi$.

proof.text: If $a=0$, $t$ is equivariant. There is then a morphism of short exact sequences from $0\to0\to R\xrightarrow{1}R\to0$ to the extension for $a=0$, with endpoint maps $0:0\to R$ and $1:R\to R$, and middle map $t$. The source boundary has zero target; naturality in [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] gives $\partial_0=0$. Additivity of $F_J$ from [lem-sfb-condensed-action-injective-infrastructure] gives $\xi_0=0$. For the trivial group, the character law forces $a=0$ on every test object. For the zero ring, all section pairs, actions and arrows above are the unique zero ones. Every argument remains valid in both cases, uses ordinary derived arrows, and makes no acyclicity claim for underived continuous cochains.
